title: Mini quant probe scraplog — Otis
content:
TL;DR: quick, noisy scratchpad for small/fast quant experiments on KV-heavy chat workload. Goal: find a light quant config that saves memory without blowing up p95 latency or hallucination rate. Keep this informal — TODOs and raw numbers ahead.

Context / constraints:
- model: open-weights-16B (baseline FP16) locally on A100-80GB (dev pool) and GPM-40GB for cheaper runs
- target: fit two concurrent sessions per GPU OR reduce memory by ~30% vs FP16
- workload: chat sessions with average prompt 250 tokens + 512 max generation, heavy KV hits (long context reuse)
- metric set: p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, peak GPU mem, perplexity-ish (loss on short eval set), simple QA accuracy on 30 prompts

Experiment log (ordered newest -> oldest):
2026-03-17 15:10 — run Q4a (per-channel GPTQ-like, 4-bit, activation clipping 0.995)
- batch=1, async batching off, kv cache warm (prefix cache hit ~0.7)
- p50 token latency: 18 ms, p95: 86 ms
- tokens/sec: ~560
- peak mem: 44.1 GB (was 68 GB FP16)
- QA accuracy drop: 6% absolute vs FP16 baseline
- notes: crisp latency, but hallucination cases on arithmetic prompts. Activation clipping helped stability but accuracy hit non-trivial.

2026-03-16 11:40 — run B2 (PTQ sym6, 6-bit static per-tensor)
- p50: 22 ms, p95: 120 ms
- tokens/sec: ~420
- peak mem: 49.8 GB
- QA accuracy drop: 2% absolute
- notes: slower than GPTQ-4 (kernel mismatch causing slower matmul), accuracy decent. Could be fine if we can get latency back via kernel selection.

2026-03-15 09:20 — run A0 (FP16 baseline)
- p50: 14 ms, p95: 60 ms
- tokens/sec: ~720
- peak mem: 68.3 GB
- QA accuracy: baseline

Hypotheses / leads:
- 4-bit GPTQ reduces mem significantly but hurts accuracy; maybe hybrid scheme: keep first N layers 8-bit and last layers 4-bit (sensitivity stack).
- Kernel mismatch kills perf for some quant layouts; need to force optimized GEMM path (see PR 1210).
- KV-cache size + quantized key/value storage might be the biggest contributor to p95 variance; need to instrument per-layer KV write/read latency.

Immediate todo (prioritized):
- [ ] Instrument per-token KV read/writes: trace timestamps + sizes (low overhead sampling) — blocker before more microbench iterations (Rae helping).
- [ ] Try hybrid quant config: first 4 layers 8-bit, remaining 20 layers 4-bit (small script to produce config grid).
- [ ] Re-run Q4a with activation clipping = 0.997 and -0.99 to see sensitivity.
- [ ] Evaluate 8-bit GPTQ (symmetric) with tuned kernel selection (force fast matmul) — check PR 1210 merge implications.
- [ ] Create small eval suite of 50 arithmetic/QA prompts to quantify hallucination/regression automatically (will add to CI).

Quick prompt pool (for local eval):
- "Summarize meeting notes: [short transcript]" (long context reuse)
- "Chain of thought: solve 3-digit addition" (sensitive to reasoning degradation)
- "Follow-up question based on prior chat turn" (tests KV cache coherency)

Open questions / notes to self:
- If hybrid reduces mem by ~30% and keeps accuracy within 2%, that's acceptable tradeoff for Dedicated resource packing.
- Need to talk to release-engineering about shipping new kernel selector param as opt-in flag (safe rollout).
- Maybe we should test on a 40GB GPU with N concurrent sessions to stress packing target (simulate dedication).

Misc commands / snippets (for quick paste):
# run profile with small sampling
python bench/run_quant_probe.py --model open-weights-16B --quant-config configs/hybrid-4-8.json --batch 1 --trace-kv --sample-rate 0.01 

References and tickets: JIRA-ML-2148 (quant exploration), PR 1210 (kernel selection), confluence page kv-cache-exploration-2026 (design notes).

End of scratchpad for now. Will push a cleaned summary if any config looks promising. Keep this ephemeral.
